correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite nontrivial G and distinct nonidentity generators, the left action is free. The quotient has exactly one orbit per level and only increasing level relations, hence is a chain. The explicit equivariant retraction sends every nonminimal level to the top level and is pointwise above the identity. Its two-level order complex is a connected bipartite graph with 2|G| vertices and |G|(r+1) edges; after the free left action there are two vertex orbits and r+1 edge orbits, giving first Betti rank r. The local neighborhood at level 1 contains two distinct minima identified by the orbit map, so the map is not a covering. The checker confirms representative groups but the general proof does not depend on enumeration.

value.rationale: The result gives a parameterized structural boundary, not a routine finite count: a free point action on a finite T0-space can have a contractible finite orbit while the geometric order-complex orbit retains first Betti rank r. It also pinpoints the mechanism by proving the finite orbit map is not a covering. This is naturally relevant to transferring equivariant information between finite spaces and simplicial realizations.
